title: Thanksgiving
subtitle: Thursday, November 26 · dinner for 7 at 4:00 PM

recipes.name: Dijon deviled eggs with crisp prosciutto and chives
ingr: about ½ tsp; family recipe says a splash
amount is our suggestion for 16 halves
recipes.done: Yolks fully set and pale yellow all the way through. Prosciutto is crisp when it snaps after cooling.
recipes.ahead: Boil, peel and make the filling Wednesday. Keep whites and filling separate, covered, in the fridge. Crisp the prosciutto Thursday morning.
recipes.store: Filling and whites: fridge up to 2 days. Assembled eggs go back in the fridge within 2 hours of coming out. Prosciutto: airtight at room temperature, same day.

steps.t: Put eggs in the saucepan, cover with cold water by an inch, and bring to a boil over high heat.
As soon as it boils, cover, turn off the heat and let the eggs sit. At Reno's elevation this takes a little longer: check one egg.
Move eggs to ice water until cold.
Peel, halve lengthwise, and pop the yolks into a bowl. Cover the whites and refrigerate.
Mash yolks with the mayo, Dijon and a splash of cider vinegar until smooth. Taste. Spoon into the piping bag, seal, refrigerate.
9:00 AM: crisp the prosciutto in a dry skillet over medium, turning once, until it darkens and stops sizzling. Drain on paper towels; it crisps as it cools. Crumble.
1:45 PM: pipe the filling into the whites. Cover and refrigerate.
2:30 PM: top with prosciutto and chives right before they go out. Back in the fridge by 4:30.

recipes.name: Ina Garten's salmon roe dip with kettle chips
recipes.gf: Dip is gluten-free; check the chips
equip: Stand mixer with paddle (or hand mixer)
ingr: fresh dill, minced, plus sprigs to garnish
from your cream; replaces the recipe's milk/half-and-half
fine Himalayan works; use a scant ¼ tsp
recipes.done: Smooth, no cream-cheese lumps; roe beads stay whole (fold, don't beat).
recipes.ahead: Make Thursday morning and keep cold. The recipe gives no make-ahead time, so same-day is the safe call.
recipes.store: Cold until serving. Out no more than 2 hours. Leftovers covered in the fridge; best the next day.

steps.t: 9:00 AM: take the cream cheese out to soften.
10:30 AM: beat the cream cheese until smooth.
On medium, mix in sour cream, lemon juice, dill, scallion, cream, salt and pepper.
Gently fold in about three-quarters of the roe with a spatula. Scrape into the serving bowl, cover, refrigerate. Keep the rest of the roe cold.
2:30 PM: top with the remaining roe and dill sprigs. Serve with chips.

recipes.name: Smoked spatchcock turkey with garlic-herb butter
recipes.passive: ≈11½ hr brine, overnight drying, ≈3½–4½ hr smoke, 30–45 min rest
equip: Poultry shears and a big cutting board
Brining bag (from the Kinder's kit) set inside a container or cooler
Rimmed baking sheet with a rack (drying, carrying)
Disposable deep roaster as a drip pan under the grate
ingr: Brine, per gallon (make enough to cover: about 2 gallons spatchcocked, 3 if it goes in whole)
on your kitchen scale; matches the recipe's 1 cup coarse kosher salt
chopped fresh parsley, thyme, chives, sage, and onion
2 tbsp go in the butter; the rest goes lightly on the outside
recipes.done: USDA: 165°F in all three places: thickest part of the breast, innermost thigh, innermost wing. The recipe's 160°F breast target is overridden. Log readings on the Turkey tab.
recipes.ahead: Spatchcock and brine Tuesday night; dry uncovered in the fridge Wednesday to Thursday morning. Butter and rub Wednesday.
recipes.store: Carve the rest off the bone, into shallow containers, in the fridge within 2 hours of serving. Eat within 3–4 days; reheat to 165°F.
flags: Homemade salt-free rub only: no commercial rub, no Kinder's seasoning packets. The Kinder's bag is a brining bag, not an oven bag. Butter stays at one stick even though the bird is bigger than the recipe's.
If it says enhanced, basted, self-basting or kosher, or lists a salt solution, the turkey is already salted. Skip the brine: pat it dry and keep it uncovered on the rack in the fridge until Thursday.

Your first salt brine (last year was buttermilk), so this uses the recipe's brine: 230 g per gallon, the usual reading of its "1 cup coarse kosher". It brines about 11½ hours (in at 9:30 PM Tuesday, out at 9 AM Wednesday) instead of the recipe's 10, so expect it a touch saltier. Weigh the salt on your kitchen scale. The drippings will be saltier than last year's, so taste before they go in the gravy.

steps.t: 8:30 PM: unwrap. Pull out the neck and giblets and any pop-up timer or leg clip; keep the neck in the fridge for the gravy. Make sure it's fully thawed (no ice inside). Read the label: if it says enhanced, basted, self-basting or kosher, or lists a salt solution, it's already salted: skip the brine (tick off the brine steps), pat it dry and keep it uncovered on the rack in the fridge until Thursday.
Mix brine: for each gallon, dissolve 230 g salt and ¾ cup brown sugar in 1 quart hot water, then add 3 quarts cold water and ice. It must be 40°F or colder before the turkey goes in.
Spatchcock: breast down, cut along both sides of the backbone with shears and remove it. Flip, press firmly on the breastbone to flatten.
9:30 PM: turkey into the brining bag, brine over it until covered, seal, into the fridge or a cooler packed with ice (check it stays at or below 40°F).

9:00 AM: lift the turkey out and discard the brine. If it went into the brine whole, spatchcock it now. Feel the cavity and thighs for ice; a little is fine, it has a full day in the fridge to finish thawing. Pat completely dry, including under the wings. Set skin-up on the rack over the sheet and refrigerate uncovered until Thursday morning.
2:30 PM: make the rub. Mash the butter with parsley, thyme, chives, sage, onion, garlic and 2 tbsp rub. Cover and refrigerate.
ing: of that rub, into the butter

steps.t: 9:00 AM: take the herb butter out to soften.

9:15 AM: fill the pellet hopper and start the smoker at 250°F. Feel inside the cavity and the thickest part of the thighs: any ice left means a longer cook, so put it on as soon as the smoker reads 250°F. Load the turkey only once the smoker reads 250°F.
9:25 AM: loosen the skin over breast, thighs and legs with your fingers. Push all the herb butter under the skin and spread it flat. Dust the outside lightly with the remaining rub.
ing: homemade rub, lightly on the outside

steps.t: 10:00 AM: turkey on the grate skin-side up, drip pan underneath. Probe in the innermost thigh, not touching bone.
Check and log the probe every hour; add pellets as needed.
About 12:30 PM (or once the thigh reads ~130°F): raise the smoker to 325–350°F to crisp the skin. From here, check every 20–30 minutes.
Done only when breast, thigh and wing all read 165°F (log all three on the Turkey tab). Expected window: 2:00–2:45 PM. It's an estimate, not a timer.

Off the smoker onto the rack, tent loosely with foil, rest 30–45 minutes. Drippings to the gravy cook. Set the smoker to its lowest setting (200–225°F): it becomes the hot hold for the stuffing and green beans.
3:20 PM: carve. Legs off, split drums and thighs, wings off, lift each breast half off in one piece and slice across. Platter, foil, into the 200°F smoker hold until 3:55.

recipes.name: Gluten-free turkey gravy, served separately
ingr: taste first: the turkey is brined
into the base Wednesday. Keep 1 more cup for Thursday, in case the drippings are short or it needs loosening
recipes.done: Wednesday: thick enough to coat a spoon (thicker than gravy; the drippings thin it Thursday). Thursday: brought to a full boil, then kept hot (140°F or hotter) on the lowest burner until serving.
recipes.ahead: Base made Wednesday at 4:00 PM (roux, broth, herbs), cooled and refrigerated. Thursday at 2:50 PM: rewarm it, whisk in the tasted drippings, and bring it to a full boil.
recipes.store: Leftovers: fridge within 2 hours, 3–4 days; reheat to a rolling boil.
flags: Skim the fat, then taste before measuring them in. If they're very salty, use less and make up the difference with broth.

steps.t: 4:00 PM (burner 4): melt the butter over medium, whisk in the gluten-free flour, and cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the 2 cups of broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring, until it's thick enough to coat a spoon. It should be thicker than gravy: Thursday's drippings thin it.
Stir in the thyme and sage; simmer 5 more minutes. No salt yet: the drippings are salty from the brine.
Pour into a shallow container; cool up to 30 minutes, then cover and refrigerate. Label it "Gravy base · Thu 2:50".
2:45 PM: pour the drippings into the fat separator. Taste them.
2:50 PM (burner 4): gravy base into the saucepan over medium; whisk as it melts and loosens. Whisk in the drippings, less if they're very salty (short on drippings? make it up with broth).
ing: broth, only if the drippings are short

steps.t: Bring it to a full boil, stirring, then simmer 3–5 minutes. Loosen with broth if it's thick; season to taste.
Hold on the lowest heat, stirring now and then.
3:50 PM: into the gravy boat. Served separately.

recipes.name: Great-Grandma Pesch's sage stuffing
recipes.passive: Bread drying whole on the counter (≈48 hr); ≈55 min bake
equip: Buttered casserole (your own; deep 13×9 or larger)
ingr: dried whole, then broken into pieces Thursday
plus a little for the dish
our practical estimate (≈8–10 hearts), not a family measurement. Hearts only; no gizzards.
our practical estimate (≈2–3 livers), not a family measurement
add gradually by how the bread absorbs it. 4–6 cups is the shopping allowance, not a pour.
recipes.done: Center reads 165°F (USDA) and the top is crisp at the edges.
recipes.ahead: The loaves dry whole on the counter from Tuesday night to Thursday (about 48 hours), then get broken into pieces. Wednesday: cook the butter, onion, celery and organs (the 'wet' mix) and refrigerate. Combine with bread and broth only right before baking: USDA says never refrigerate mixed, uncooked stuffing.
recipes.store: Leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours; fridge 3–4 days; reheat to 165°F.
flags: The family recipe gives no organ amounts. About ¼ lb each of hearts and liver is our practical starting point; adjust to taste. Broth goes in gradually.
The family recipe doesn't say. We scheduled 350°F: ≈35 min covered, then ≈20 uncovered, until the center reads 165°F.

steps.t: 9:00 PM: take both loaves out of their bags and leave them out on the counter, uncovered, to dry whole until Thursday (about 48 hours).
11:00 AM: melt the butter; cook onion and celery until soft.
Add the minced hearts and liver and cook until no pink remains and the largest piece reads 165°F. Season with dried parsley, sage and salt. Cool in a shallow container; refrigerate.
1:30 PM: break the dried loaves into bite-size pieces into the big bowl.
1:30 PM: warm the wet mix gently until the butter melts.
1:45 PM: in the big bowl, toss bread with the wet mix. Add broth a cup at a time until evenly moist. Taste for salt. Pack into the buttered casserole; cover with foil.
2:05 PM: bake at 350°F, covered.
2:40 PM: uncover and bake until the center reads 165°F and the top crisps.
3:00 PM: out, covered, into the smoker hot hold (200–225°F). Check it reads 140°F or hotter at 3:30 and 3:50.

recipes.name: Kenji's green bean casserole
equip: 13×9 baking dish (disposable, on a sheet pan)
ingr: the recipe's 2 tsp is for regular soy; dark is stronger, so start with half and taste
1 cup folded in; 1 cup on top at serving
recipes.done: Bubbling at the edges and hot through after the covered and uncovered stages.
recipes.ahead: Assemble Wednesday; cool, cover, refrigerate. Thursday: about 30 minutes covered + 10 uncovered at 350°F from cold.
recipes.store: Leftovers: fridge within 2 hours, 3–4 days; reheat to 165°F.
flags: You have dark soy, which is stronger and darker than regular, so the amount is halved to 1 tsp. Taste the sauce and add more only if it needs it.
Gluten-free flour, neutral oil with the butter, purchased crispy onions (no shallot frying). Not gluten-free because of the onions.

steps.t: 12:00 PM: big pot of salted water to a boil (it takes longer at Reno's elevation).
Blanch the beans 5 minutes, then into ice water. Drain well.
Sauté the mushrooms in the butter and oil until their liquid is gone and they brown.
Add garlic for 30 seconds, then the gluten-free flour for 1–2 minutes, stirring.
Whisk in the broth, cream, soy sauce and lemon juice; simmer 5 minutes. Season.
Fold in the beans and 1 cup crispy onions. Into the 13×9. Cool about 30 minutes, then cover and refrigerate.
2:30 PM: into the 350°F oven, covered with foil.

3:00 PM: check the center reads 165°F (it was made Wednesday). If not, leave it in, covered, while the oven heats for the mac, and check every 5 minutes; out by 3:10. Then, still covered, into the smoker hot hold (200–225°F).
3:40 PM: back in the oven, uncovered, until bubbling. The oven is cooling from 425°F and still hotter than 350°F, so look at 5 minutes.
3:50 PM: top with the remaining 1 cup crispy onions right before serving.

recipes.name: Momofuku Brussels sprouts with mint
recipes.passive: Boil earlier, char at the end
ingr: the recipe starts with them already cooked
1 tbsp for the cereal; 1 tbsp split across the charring batches
recipes.done: Sprouts tender with deeply charred cut sides. Dress with only enough to coat.
recipes.ahead: Wednesday: dressing base (no herbs), refrigerated; toast the cereal with cayenne, cool, store airtight. Thursday: boil and dry the sprouts, char at the end.
recipes.store: Best right away. Leftovers: fridge within 2 hours.
flags: The recipe assumes cooked sprouts and doesn't say how. Our plan: boil until just tender, starting checks at 4–6 minutes (size matters), then drain and dry well.
Don't crowd the skillet. Two batches of about 5 minutes each, oil split between them.

steps.t: 3:30 PM: mix fish sauce, water, sugar, rice vinegar, lime juice, garlic and chile until the sugar dissolves. Refrigerate (no herbs yet).
Toast the rice crisps with the cayenne and a pinch of salt in 1 tbsp oil, about 30 seconds. Cool completely; store airtight.
12:00 PM (our method): boil the sprouts in salted water until just tender.
Drain, spread on towels to dry thoroughly, then refrigerate.
3:30 PM: chop the cilantro and mint; stir into the dressing.
3:40 PM (burner 5, batch 1): very hot skillet, half the remaining oil, half the sprouts cut-side down. Char without stirring.
Batch 2 the same way.
3:52 PM: toss with just enough dressing to coat. Crispy rice in its own dish on the side.
ing: rice crisps, in their own dish

recipes.name: Brown-butter mashed red potatoes
recipes.tag: For the Love of Cooking, your version
equip: Small light-colored saucepan (to see the butter brown)
recipes.done: A knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.
recipes.ahead: Cut Thursday 1:15 PM and hold in cold water in the fridge. Cook at the end.
recipes.store: Hold covered on the lowest burner up to ~30 min, stirring; loosen with hot water. Leftovers: fridge within 2 hours; reheat to 165°F.
flags: No pepper, chives, garlic, onion or stock. Gravy stays separate.

steps.t: 1:15 PM: cut the potatoes; cover with cold water; refrigerate.
2:40 PM: drain, cover with fresh cold water, salt it, and bring to a boil.
3:00 PM: simmer until tender (allow extra time at Reno's elevation).
Meanwhile brown the butter over medium until nutty and amber. Watch closely; pull it right away.
Save 1½ cups of the hot cooking water, then drain. Back in the pot: pour in the brown butter, mash coarsely, add hot water a splash at a time, salt to taste.
Cover; hold on burner 1 at the lowest heat until 3:55, stirring once or twice. It should stay steaming (140°F or hotter).

recipes.name: Rob Li's gochujang lobster mac and cheese
equip: Disposable 13×9 on a sheet pan (or a 2–3 qt dish)
ingr: salted: taste before adding any salt
weigh dry, then cook: our planning choice
recipes.done: Bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
recipes.ahead: Cook and chop the lobster and shred the cheeses Wednesday. Toast the panko Wednesday (store airtight; fold in parsley Thursday). Sauce, pasta and bake happen Thursday.
recipes.store: Leftovers in the fridge within 2 hours; eat within 2 days (seafood); reheat to 165°F.
flags: Fried shallots, MSG, extra egg yolk, truffle, caviar. Usual heat level; both gochujang and gochugaru stay.

steps.t: 10:30 AM: boil the lobster tails in salted water until the shells are bright red and the meat is opaque and firm all the way through. Ice, then pull the meat, chop, refrigerate.
Shred the cheddar and gruyère; grate the pecorino. Refrigerate.
3:45 PM: topping. Sauté shallot, garlic and thyme in butter and oil, add the GF panko and toast until golden. Cool; store airtight.
2:35 PM: pasta water on (salted).
2:40 PM: sauce. Sauté shallot, garlic and thyme in butter and oil 2–3 min; stir in gochujang and gochugaru; add the cooking sherry and reduce by about a third.
Add the cream and simmer until reduced by about a third.
Off the heat: stir in cheddar and gruyère in three additions, then mascarpone. Add Worcestershire and hot sauce. Taste, then salt only if needed.
2:52 PM: cook the elbows about 2 minutes short of the box's al dente time. Drain.
tm: Pasta: 2 min short of al dente

steps.t: 3:03 PM: layer in the dish: half the pasta, half the sauce, all the lobster, the rest of the pasta and sauce, then the topping cheeses.
3:12 PM: bake at 425°F.

3:35 PM: out. Check the center reads 165°F (the lobster went in cold from the fridge); if not, back in for 5 minutes and check again. Fold parsley into the panko; scatter on with chives. Tent loosely with foil and rest until 3:55 (it sets the sauce).

recipes.name: Orange cranberry sauce (original orange/maple)
recipes.done: Berries popped; thick enough to coat a spoon (it thickens more as it cools).
recipes.ahead: Make Wednesday (up to 3 days ahead is fine).
recipes.store: Airtight in the fridge 3–5 days; freezes up to 2 months.
flags: No alcohol, no spicy version. Bottled orange juice was ordered but isn't used unless you say so.

steps.t: 9:00 AM: combine cranberries, orange juice, maple syrup and vanilla in the pot (save the zest). Bring to a boil over medium-high.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer until berries pop and it coats a spoon.
Uncover and simmer a few more minutes to thicken.
Cool, then into an airtight container in the fridge.
3:00 PM: out of the fridge.
3:50 PM: into the bowl; zest on top.

recipes.name: Via Carota–inspired green salad
ingr: from the package; you won't need all of them
the bag has 3; the third is spare
recipes.done: Leaves completely dry before dressing; tossed only right before plating.
recipes.ahead: Vinaigrette Wednesday (keeps up to 3 days in the fridge). Wash and dry greens Thursday at noon.
recipes.store: Undressed greens keep a day in towels; dressed salad doesn't keep.
flags: Set aside plain lettuce for Mom before any seasoning or dressing.
Add dressing gradually; you won't use the whole batch.

steps.t: 3:30 PM: rinse the chopped shallot in a strainer; drain.
Combine shallot, garlic, sugar, salt, thyme, sherry vinegar and warm water. Slowly whisk in the oil. Refrigerate.
12:00 PM: wash the lettuces; spin or towel completely dry; roll in towels; refrigerate.
3:00 PM: vinaigrette out of the fridge; whisk again before using.
3:45 PM: slice the endive. Set aside plain lettuce for Mom first.
3:52 PM: toss the rest with dressing a little at a time; plate.

recipes.name: Paula Deen's pumpkin gooey butter cake
equip: Disposable 13×9 on a sheet pan (lightly greased)
ingr: King Arthur GF yellow cake mix
weigh it from the 22-oz box; save the rest
recipes.done: Edges set and golden; center still a little gooey with a slight jiggle. Don't overbake.
recipes.ahead: Bake Wednesday. It cuts cleaner after a night in the fridge.
recipes.store: Cream cheese and eggs make it perishable: cool, cover, refrigerate. Out no more than 2 hours. Fridge 3–4 days.
flags: Use these ingredients, not the cake-mix box's directions. No milk or buttermilk. Don't apply the box's high-altitude changes; go by the jiggle.

steps.t: 12:55 PM: heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the 13×9. Start the crust while it heats.
Mix the 18¼ oz cake mix, 1 egg and 8 tbsp melted butter; pat evenly into the pan.
Beat cream cheese and pumpkin smooth. Beat in 3 eggs, vanilla and melted butter. Mix in powdered sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg.
1:20 PM: spread the filling over the crust and bake.
Pull when the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly. Cool on a rack, then cover and refrigerate.
≈4:45 PM: out of the fridge 30 minutes before dessert (if you like it less cold). Cut into squares.

tasks.text: Unwrap the turkey, giblets out, and read the label (already salted? skip the brine).
tips: Still partly icy?

Normal for a fresh bird kept near 26°F. Loosen stuck giblets with a minute of cold tap water in the cavity, then brine as planned in the fridge or an iced cooler at 40°F or colder: the cold brine finishes the thaw. Don't thaw it in a sink of water; USDA says a cold-water-thawed turkey must be cooked right away. Frozen hard all the way through? Stop and ask Claude: the plan changes.

tasks.text: Mix brine (230 g salt + ¾ cup brown sugar per gallon) and get it to 40°F or colder by 9:30 (lots of ice).
Spatchcock the turkey.
tips: Backbone too stiff to cut?

Don't force the shears. Brine it whole tonight (mix 3 gallons instead of 2, same strength) and spatchcock it Wednesday at 9:00 when it comes out of the brine. Lay it on the clean smoker grate once, whenever you spatchcock, to check it fits.

tasks.text: Bread out of the bags; leave both loaves out on the counter to dry whole until Thursday.
Turkey into the brine (fridge, or cooler with ice at 40°F or colder).
Clear one full fridge shelf for the turkey's drying tray (from Wednesday 9:00).
Turkey out of brine, patted very dry, uncovered on a rack in the fridge until Thursday.
Cranberry sauce; cool; fridge.
Hard-boil eggs (check one at 14 min), ice, peel; filling; fridge separately.
Lobster tails, ice, chop, fridge. Shred and grate cheeses.
Stuffing wet mix (butter, onion, celery, hearts, liver to 165°F); cool in a shallow container; fridge.
Green bean casserole: boil water, blanch, sauce, assemble; cool 30 min; fridge.
Oven to 350°F; gooey butter cake in at 1:20; check at 2:00; cool; fridge.
Salt-free rub; one-stick garlic-herb butter; fridge.
Sherry vinaigrette; fridge.
Sprouts dressing base (no herbs); toast rice crisps with cayenne; cool; airtight.
GF panko topping; cool; airtight.
Burner 4: gravy base (roux, broth, herbs; no drippings, no salt); cool; fridge.
Pellets: full hopper plus a spare bag for Thursday's smoke and 200°F hot hold.
Fridge plan for Thursday; label each dish with its pull time.
Cream cheese out of the fridge to soften.
Herb butter out of the fridge to soften.
Crisp the prosciutto; drain; airtight at room temperature.
Fill hopper; smoker to 250°F.
Herb butter under the skin; rub lightly outside.
Turkey on, skin up, drip pan below, probe in the thigh.
tips: Smoker trouble?
Turkey to the oven at 350°F on its sheet pan; stuffing and green beans to the cooler hot box; mac bakes after.

tasks.text: Make the roe dip (¾ of the roe folded in); cover; fridge.
Log temperature; check pellets.
Sprouts: boil until just tender (our method), dry well, fridge.
Wash and dry greens; roll in towels; fridge.
Set out every serving bowl, platter, utensil and the gravy boat; put a note on each with its dish. Plates and napkins on the table.
Log temperature. If the thigh is about 130°F, raise the smoker to 325–350°F now.
Smoker at 325–350°F (crisp skin). Check every 20–30 min from now.
Cut potatoes; cold water; fridge.
Break the dried bread into pieces; warm the wet mix until the butter melts.
Pipe deviled eggs; cover; fridge.
Mix stuffing (bread + wet mix + broth added gradually); taste; into buttered casserole; foil on.
Oven to 350°F for the stuffing and green beans.
Turkey done window opens (2:00–2:45). Done only at 165°F in breast, thigh and wing.
tips: Turkey done early?
Rest it tented 30 minutes, then foil and into the smoker at 200°F (or the cooler hot box). Check it stays 140°F or hotter. Carve at 3:20 as planned.
Turkey running late?

1:45 PM, breast under 145°F: smoker to 350°F now. 2:45 PM, any spot under 155°F: keep going; sides hold in the cooler hot box. 3:15 PM, still not 165°F everywhere: cut off the leg quarters, or move it to the oven after the mac (3:35, at 350–425°F). Push dinner to 4:30 rather than serve it under 165°F.

tasks.text: Stuffing in, covered.
Green bean casserole in from the fridge, covered.
Deviled eggs out: top with prosciutto and chives.
Roe dip out: top it; chips alongside.
Burner 2: pasta water on.
Uncover stuffing; bake to 165°F in the center.
tips: Not 165°F by 3:00?
Leave it in while the oven climbs to 425°F; it fits beside the mac. Pull it at 165°F, then into the hold.

tasks.text: Burner 1: potato water on.
Burner 3: mac sauce.
Turkey off once it's 165°F everywhere: tent, rest. Smoker to its lowest setting for the hot hold (aim 200–225°F); open the lid a few minutes so it drops faster.
tips: Not 165°F everywhere yet?

1:45 PM, breast under 145°F: smoker to 350°F now. 2:45 PM, any spot under 155°F: keep going; sides hold in the cooler hot box. 3:15 PM, still not 165°F everywhere: cut off the leg quarters, or move it to the oven after the mac (3:35, at 350–425°F). Push dinner to 4:30 rather than serve it under 165°F.

tasks.text: Burner 4: rewarm the gravy base, whisk in the drippings (taste first), full boil; hold on lowest.
tips: Not much drippings?
Whisk 1 cup broth into the base instead; that's why a cup of broth is held back.

tasks.text: Burner 2: elbows in, 2 min short of al dente.
tm: Pasta: 2 min short of al dente

tasks.text: Stuffing (165°F) out, covered, into the 200°F smoker hold.
tips: Smoker not free or not holding 200°F?

Hot-hold backup: a dry cooler, preheated with hot water for 10 minutes then dried, lined with towels. Pans go in covered; check 140°F or hotter at 3:30 and 3:50. Reheat anything that drops below to 165°F.

tasks.text: Green beans out, covered, into the smoker hold.
tips: Smoker not free or not holding 200°F?

Hot-hold backup: a dry cooler, preheated with hot water for 10 minutes then dried, lined with towels. Pans go in covered; check 140°F or hotter at 3:30 and 3:50. Reheat anything that drops below to 165°F.

tasks.text: Oven up to 425°F for the mac.
Burner 1: potatoes in.
Cranberry sauce out of the fridge.
Vinaigrette out of the fridge.
Assemble the mac and cheese.
Mac in at 425°F.
Burner 3: brown butter. Drain potatoes (save water); mash; hold covered on burner 1, lowest.
Carve; platter; foil; into the 200°F smoker hold.
Hot-hold check: stuffing and green beans read 140°F or hotter.
Chop the cilantro and mint into the sprouts dressing.
Mac out; panko + chives on; tent loosely with foil. Oven off, door cracked so it falls toward 350°F.
Green beans back in uncovered. The oven is still hotter than 350°F, so look at 5 minutes.
Burner 5: char sprouts, batch 1 then 2.
Slice endive; plain lettuce for Mom first.
Toss the salad and plate it.
Dress the sprouts lightly (rice on the side).
Crispy onions on the green beans.
Gravy into the boat.
Cranberry sauce into the bowl; zest on top.
Spot-check every hot dish: 140°F or hotter. Anything cooler gets reheated to 165°F (covered, in the microwave or the oven), checked again, then served. Dinner can wait a few minutes.
Dinner. Sit down; anything still cooking can wait for you.
Two-hour rule: deviled eggs back in the fridge.
Two-hour rule: roe dip back in the fridge.
